title: AlphaFold2-guided mining identifies context-independent cytidine deaminases for efficient base editing
summary: Researchers used AlphaFold2 to predict structures for 1,483 cytidine deaminases, clustered the predictions and experimentally characterized representatives. The screen identified previously uncharacterized enzymes with high editing efficiency, and CD0208^P52A showed little sequence-context preference across AC/GC/TC/CC motifs, a narrow editing window and relatively low off-target activity. In mammalian cells, its base editor introduced stop codons in single- and multicopy genes without DNA double-strand breaks.
ai_technology: AlphaFold2 protein-structure prediction, followed by structural clustering of candidate cytidine deaminases
organization: Agricultural Genomics Institute at Shenzhen, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

evidence.tested: Researchers used AlphaFold2 to predict structures for 1,483 cytidine deaminases, clustered the predictions and experimentally characterized representatives.
evidence.unknown: The base-editing experiments were preclinical cell experiments, not animal or clinical efficacy tests. AlphaFold2 supplied predicted rather than experimentally solved structures. The paper reports multiple promising deaminases; CD0208^P52A is the specific context-independent editor highlighted here. No therapeutic safety or in-vivo delivery claim is implied.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold2-predicted structures at scale were used to mine and cluster 1,483 putative deaminases; representatives were then selected for experimental characterization in cytosine base editors. The model enabled structure-guided candidate selection; editing outcomes were measured experimentally in mammalian cells.
